title: Adjoin one prescribed residue-field element by a flat local extension
statement: theorem exists_flat_local_monogenic_extension (A : Type (max u v)) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (K : Type v) [Field K] (ψ : A →+* K) (hker : RingHom.ker ψ = maximalIdeal A) (x : K) : ∃ (B : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : IsLocalRing B) (_ : Algebra A B) (φ : B →+* K), (algebraMap A B).Flat ∧ (maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A B) = maximalIdeal B ∧ RingHom.ker φ = maximalIdeal B ∧ φ.comp (algebraMap A B) = ψ ∧ ∃ b, φ b = x

source.place: first proof paragraph (the monogenic construction); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03C3

proof.text: The image F of ψ is a field, since ker ψ is the maximal ideal of A and the quotient A/ker ψ is its residue field. If x is transcendental over F, evaluate A[T] at x and localize at the ideal of polynomials whose coefficients lie in the maximal ideal of A. Transcendence identifies this ideal with the evaluation kernel, so it is prime and evaluation extends to the localization. This localization is local, with maximal ideal generated by that of A, and its evaluation kernel is that maximal ideal. A[T] is free over A and localization is flat, so the composite is flat. The class of T maps to x. If x is algebraic over F, lift the coefficients of its monic minimal polynomial to A and take B = A[T]/(the lifted monic polynomial). The power basis makes B finite free, hence flat over A. Evaluation descends. Polynomial division by the monic polynomial shows its kernel is exactly the extended maximal ideal of A, and its image is the field F(x). Thus this ideal is maximal. Every maximal ideal of B contracts to the maximal ideal of A because B is integral over A; it therefore contains, and equals, the extended ideal. Hence B is local. Again the class of T maps to x. Both constructions have carriers in Type (max u v), the universe of A.
